Then, the solution of Equation (19) satisfies

\[ I_{10}(5) = e^{-4\gamma T}I_{10}(1) + \frac{1}{\mu_{10}} \left( s_{10} T + x_{10} T_{27} \right) \left( 1 - e^{-4\gamma T} \right). \]

From the profile of PICTIL/IL-27 in Figure 3D of [30], we have \( I_{10}(1) = 400pg/cm^3 \) at day 1 and \( I_{10}(5) = 1800pg/cm^3 \) at day 5, so that

\[ 1800pg/cm^3 = e^{-4\gamma \times 16/day} \times 400pg/cm^3 \]

\[ + \frac{1}{16/day} \left[ 8.89 \times 10^{-8} \times 3 \times 10^8 \]

\[ + x_{10} \times 3 \times 10^8 \]

\[ \times \frac{26875pg/cm^3}{26875pg/cm^3 + 5000pg/cm^3(1 - e^{-4\gamma \times 16/day})} \right]. \]

Therefore, we take \( x_{10} = 1.128 \times 10^{-7} pg/cell/day. \)

Estimate of the parameters in (3)

From [48], we have \( \mu_T = 0.3/day. \) For J558-Ctrl tumor cells, the term of \( I_{27} \) in (3) drops out, and we consider a simplified version:

\[
\frac{dT(t)}{dt} = s_T - \frac{c}{c + c_T} \mu_T T(t),
\]

which, if c is constant, has the solution

\[
T(5) = e^{-4\gamma T(1)} + \frac{s_T c}{\mu_T (c + c_T)} \left( 1 - e^{-4\gamma T} \right).
\]

Substituting \( T(1) \) and \( T(5) \) from (15), we get

\[ 2.6 \times 10^8 cell/cm^3 = e^{-4\gamma \times 0.3/day \times 1} \times 1.1 \times 10^8 cell/cm^3 \]

\[ + \frac{s_T}{\mu_T} \frac{c}{c + c_T} \times (1 - e^{-4\gamma \times 0.3/day}). \]

Based on the fact that the (20) is close to \( 2.3 \times 10^8 \) while the (16) is close to \( 2.3 \frac{c}{c_T + c} \), we choose \( s_T = 1.3968 \times 10^8 cell/cm^3/day. \)

Next, we consider

\[
\frac{dT(t)}{dt} = \frac{s_T c}{c + c_T} - \frac{\mu_T}{1 + \frac{g_{27} I_{27} + \beta_T \sigma_T I_{10}}{T(t)}}
\]

where the solution satisfies

\[
T(5) = e^{-4\gamma T(1)} + \frac{s_T c}{w_T (c + c_T)} \left( 1 - e^{-4\gamma T} \right)
\]

with \( w_T = \frac{\mu_T}{1 + \sigma_T I_{27} + \beta_T \sigma_T I_{10}}. \) Recalling \( T(1) \) and \( T(5) \) from (16), we get

\[
(5 - e^{-4\gamma T}) \times 10^8 cell/cm^3 = \frac{1.3968 \times 10^8}{w_T}
\]

\[ \times (1 - e^{-4\gamma T}) \times \frac{c}{c + c_T}. \]

In (22), the left-hand side is close to \( 5 \times 10^8 \) and the right-hand side is close to \( 5.52 \times \frac{c}{c + c_T} \times 10^8, \) while we take \( \sigma_T = 2 \times 10^{-4} pg/cm^3 \) and \( \beta_T = 9. \)

Estimate of the parameters in (4)

We assume that the diffusion coefficient of \( I_f \) is the same as that of \( I_{27}, \) namely, \( D_f = 1.25 \times 10^{-3} cm^2/day. \) Next we use the simplified version:

\[
\frac{dI_f(t)}{dt} = \frac{x_T s_T}{s_T + I_{27}} - \mu_f I_f(t),
\]

where \( \mu_f = 2.16/day \) by [49]. For tumor cells J558-Ctrl (which do not generate \( I_{27} \)), (23) reduces to

\[
\frac{dI_f(t)}{dt} = x_T T - \mu_f I_f(t).
\]

If \( T \) is constant, then the solution of (24) satisfies

\[
I_f(5) = e^{-\mu_f T(1)} I_f(1) + \frac{x_T}{\mu_f} \left( 1 - e^{-\mu_f T} \right).
\]

Taking \( T \) to be the average of \( T(1) \) and \( T(5) \) in (15) and taking \( I_f(1) \) from the curve PICTIL in the right part of Figure 3D in [30], we have

\[ 3100pg/cm^3 = e^{-4\gamma \times 2.16/day \times 250pg/cm^3} \]

\[ + x_T \times 1.8 \times 10^8 cell/cm^3 \times \frac{1}{2.16/day} \times (1 - e^{-4\gamma \times 2.16/day}), \]

so that \( x_T = 3.72 \times 10^{-7} pg/cell/day. \) We choose \( s_T = 5 \times 10^8 pg/cm^3. \)

Estimate of the parameters in (5)

We consider a simplified version of (5):

\[
\frac{dc(t)}{dt} = \lambda_{c}(1) - \mu_{c}(t) - \frac{I_{10}}{I_{10} + \sigma_{c}} - \eta_{f} \frac{I_{f}}{I_{f} + s_{c}} c(t).
\]

We choose \( s_c = 300pg/cm^3. \) In order to compute \( \eta_f, \) we consider T cells IL-10^-/PICTIL and IL-10^-/PICTIL/IL-27 which do not generate \( I_{10}, \) so that \( I_{10} \) drops out of Equation (25):

\[
\frac{dc(t)}{dt} = \lambda_{c}(1) - \mu_{c}(t) - \eta_{f} \frac{I_{f}}{I_{f} + s_{c}} c(t).
\]
